# Capability: pieces

The contract of this folder is [`specs/pieces/pieces.md`](../../specs/pieces/pieces.md), `CAP-PCS`. Read it before a change
to what this capability does. A test title cites each criterion it verifies: `AC-PCS-###`.
The rules for all of `src/` are in [`src/AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md).

> Applies to `src/pieces/**`, `src/musical-model/**`, `src/circuit/**`, `src/board-editing/placement.ts`.

# The model

The contracts say what these modules do: [pieces](../../specs/pieces/pieces.md),
[musical model](../../specs/musical-model/musical-model.md) and
[circuit](../../specs/circuit/circuit.md). This file holds what they do not say.

Run `check_invariants` of the `pentomino-domain` MCP server before and after a change to the
geometry, to `SHAPES` or to the musical model. It runs the checks on the 96 orientations and
returns counterexamples.

## Traps

Each one compiles and passes the typecheck. The result is a wrong board or a wrong sound, with no
error.

- **A cell is its index.** `rotate90`, `normalize`, `reflect` and `cellsAt` are each a `map`, so
  cell `k` of a shape is cell `k` in each orientation and on the board. The grip cell
  (`ANCHOR_INDEX`), the degree, the step and the two gates are read by that index. Do not filter,
  sort or regroup cells in those functions: write a new function. `checkArrayOrder` is the net.
- **`y` grows downward.** These are grid coordinates, so an angle grows clockwise on screen. Do not
  correct it.
- **Compute the degree and the step on `SHAPES[piece]`, never on `p.cells`.**
  `degreeByCellIndex` and `playOrderByCellIndex` take the shape with no orientation, and the
  result travels by index. On an oriented shape they give another mapping in 53 of the 96
  orientations.
- **A cell has two numbers.** The degree says which note: read `notesForRotation(...)[degree]`,
  the ascending arpeggio. The step says when: read `arpeggioFor(...)[step]`, which has the
  retrograde applied. A reflection moves the step and not the degree. The ascending arpeggio read
  by step gives the mirrored note in each reflected piece.
- **Two tables are the inverse of two others.** `pathThroughCells` and `cellsByPlayOrder` give the
  cell at each position. `degreeByCellIndex` and `playOrderByCellIndex` give the position of each
  cell. All four are permutations of `0..4`.
- **The cost chooses, and the moves give the time.** A crossing costs `CROSS_COST` and lasts one
  interval. An offset and the cycle length read `steps`, never `cost`.
- **A packed key must not carry.** `PASOS_MAX` in `sequence.ts` and `BASE` in `transform.ts` are
  greater than the sum over the whole circuit or the whole walk, not over one leg or one move. A
  smaller value reorders the result.
- **Pass the regime on.** No function has a default regime, and none chooses one. A fixed regime
  gives another note in 36 of the 48 combinations of piece and rotation.
- **The letter names the shape, not the sound.** Piece `F` has tonic C. Note F is the tonic of
  piece `T`.

## Decisions to test a change against

- **The shape decides inside a piece.** The position of a piece and its neighbours never change
  its notes, its degrees or its gates.
  [Why](../../docs/architecture/decisions/2026-10-04-the-shape-decides-inside-a-piece.md)
- **The circuit is exact.** `MAX_PIEZAS` is a rule, not the area of the board. Do not raise it.
  [Why](../../docs/architecture/decisions/2026-10-04-exact-circuit-and-a-piece-limit-of-twelve.md)
- **The arpeggio walks the piece.** A diagonal move exists only inside a piece. `routeBetween`
  moves by sides.
  [Why](../../docs/architecture/decisions/2026-10-04-the-arpeggio-walks-the-piece.md)
